items.title: ❗️The EU rejected Kyiv’s request to bring forward additional funding from 2027, the Financial Times reports. Brussels is instead pressing Ukraine to implement agreed reforms that could unlock around €34 billion in support before year-end. Requirements cited include ending a tax exemption for small international parcels and introducing new taxation rules for digital platforms. The European Commission also warned against reversing previously implemented commitments. #EU

items.title: Moldova confirmed drone debris at multiple locations after five Russian attack UAVs crossed its airspace between 07:45 and 08:00. Fragments were found near Căușeni, Dubovca in Hîncești, Crocmaz in Ștefan Vodă, and between Delacău and Puhăceni in Anenii Noi. Near Crocmaz, an explosion in a vineyard caused a vegetation fire and damaged windows at a nearby agricultural facility. Preliminary reports indicate no casualties. #Moldova

items.title: ❗️The US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund has signed its first critical minerals deal, Reuters reports. Around $30 million will be invested in a joint platform with BGV Group focused initially on early-stage Ukrainian mining projects involving rare earths, uranium, beryllium and zirconium. The fund has also launched four other projects, including two aimed at strengthening Ukraine’s electricity and heating networks ahead of winter. #Ukraine

items.title: Ukraine’s General Staff says Defense Forces struck several Russian military targets on October 2 and overnight into October 3. A strike-drone storage, preparation and launch site was hit near occupied Donetsk, along with a command post near Nova Tavolzhanka in Russia’s Belgorod region and a crossing over the Mokri Yaly River near Novoocheretuvate. A Russian repair base in Kherson region and a logistics depot in Belgorod region were also hit. #Ukraine

Impacts were recorded at 12 locations and debris at five, while several drones remained airborne at 09:00. #Ukraine

items.summary:
New Russian systems 1/2
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
A new Russian Pantsir-S1M air defense system mounted on a Belarusian MZKT-7930-312 wheeled chassis appeared during the Center-2026 exercises. Earlier reporting from a Belarusian opposition source said MZKT received a contract in early 2024 to manufacture 18 MZKT-7930-312 chassis for Russian Pantsir combat modules. Russia’s KBP reportedly notified MZKT on August 15, 2024 that testing of the 72V6.00.00.000-08 combat module on the chassis was completed successfully. #Russia

items.title: R to @NOELreports: Japan might supply Ukraine with weapons and interceptors.
items.summary:
Japan might supply Ukraine with weapons and interceptors.
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
❗️Japan plans to reopen discussions on providing or selling weapons to Ukraine, including Patriot interceptors, according to former Defense Minister Itsunori Onodera. Japan operates 24 Patriot batteries and domestically manufactures PAC-3 interceptors under license from Lockheed Martin. Onodera said legal and government policy restrictions remain, but Tokyo intends to begin internal discussions on possible next steps following his visit to Kyiv. #Ukraine

items.summary:
Lets continue with the general events. Another Russian drone entered Romania
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
Romania’s Defense Ministry reported that an object, possibly an aerial drone, fell near Plauru in Tulcea County around 05:00 as drones attacked targets in Ukraine near the Romanian border. The object started a fire, but no casualties or material damage were reported. Romanian authorities secured the area and launched an investigation. The ministry said its radars detected no unauthorized incursion into Romanian airspace. #Ukraine

items.title: Must-read about why the oil is flowing now but prices are still going up 👇
items.summary:
Must-read about why the oil is flowing now but prices are still going up 👇
Philippe Lemoine (@phl43)
I think it's true that crude flows through Hormuz are more or less back to pre-war volumes, people who think it's some kind of propaganda campaign orchestrated by the Trump administration that somehow managed to get independent analysts like Kpler on board are delusional, but the US hasn't won anything.
First, although volumes are back to pre-war levels, price isn't because this has been achieved by a complex and very expensive system of shuttle tankers to get the oil out of Hormuz and ship-to-ship transfers to move it to its final destination and insurance costs have skyrocketed because risks are still very elevated, so the cost of moving oil out of the Gulf is now $30-$35 per barrel compared to less than $7 before the war according to Reuters.
Since moreover inventories have been depleted everywhere, there is strong upward pressure on demand and this will remain the case for a while even if the US can keep the volumes of crude flowing through Hormuz at this level, which explains why the Brent is still hovering around $100/barrel and will likely continue to do so for several months, compared to ~$70 before the war. This means the worst case scenario will likely be avoided, but that's hardly a victory.
But perhaps more importantly, people and businesses don't consume crude, they consume refined products and their price is still very high and rising, because unlike crude the flows of refined products through Hormuz still haven't recovered (they're down to ~600,000 barrels from ~$3.6 million before the war according to Kpler), Russia stopped exporting because Ukrainian attacks on its refineries cut its production capacity and inventories are depleted everywhere. This will also continue for the foreseeable future.
The US has severely depleted its stockpiles of interceptors and to a lesser extent of standoff offensive munitions, had to evacuate most of its bases in the region and the blockade plus the patrols in the strait impose a heavy price on its navy. Of course, Iran is also under a lot of pressure because of the blockade, so I still expect that eventually both sides will agree to some bullshit deal that won't fundamentally solve anything but will relieve the immediate strains on their economy and military.
However, I now think it's likely there will be another round of escalation before that, because I don't think Trump will be able to wait months for the Iranian economy to collapse while the prices of refined products remain so high or get even higher and now that Iran has lost control of the strait to a large extent it has incentives to escalate to increase the pressure on Trump to make a deal.
People say that the US can simply wait Iran out until its economy collapses, but if the Iranians think that's where they're headed, they have nothing to lose and can credibly threaten to destroy energy infrastructure in the region they have mostly spared so far because they were afraid of retaliation in kind. I think that the US knows that, and that the economic deterioration will pressure Iranian hawks to moderate, so that both sides will eventually make compromises to enable some kind of deal.
Whatever this deal is, I don't think it will even come close to initial US objectives, which let's be real was to overthrow the regime or at least force it to capitulate and do a wholesale change of its foreign policy like Venezuela after Maduro's abduction. Iran will not abandon its hostility to the US and Israel, it will keep its ballistic missile program and drones, the regime will stay in place and its nuclear program will remain a point of contention with the US and Israel for many years.
It's hard to predict how this will end exactly because Trump created a situation that is very difficult to unfuck, so maybe I'm wrong, but even if I turn out to be wrong in the end we don't know that yet and the victory laps that plan trusters are taking right now are premature and frankly ridiculous given what a disaster this war has been so far. It's like we're back at the beginning of March, they just never learn.
If the US had been able to restore a semi-normal situation in Hormuz by April, maybe it would have been a different story, but it wasn't and now it's objectively in a much worse situation than it was before the war and hasn't obtained anything from Iran yet, so I don't know what this amazing victory people are talking about is supposed to be. They just never learn.
— https://nitter.kareem.one/phl43/status/2106052652517748777#m

items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: Dobropilla - the biggest ongoing battle of the Ukrainian 🇺🇦 war The scale of the battle for Dobropilla has rarely been seen before. Russian 🇷🇺 forces are sending hundreds of men on assault everyday, hundreds are being eliminated while the 1st Azov Corps still manages to contain the offensive. Russia is currently massing 4 armies on a 50km front to attack Dobropilla and advance west of Kramatorsk, the main key city under Ukrainian control in the Donbas. In this direction, Russia is using a massive number of drones and KAB guided bombs, as well as many soldiers. In recent weeks, they managed to advance south of Dobropilla and secure a foothold north and west of the defensive line 0.5 (incomplete). Despite heavy losses, they advanced (mainly the 51st army) and are threatening the city from the south. Further north, the 41st army didn't manage to progress a lot, despite a lot of infiltrations. They suffered from recent counter-attacks from Ukrainian forces, which managed to clear some infiltrated areas. Right now, the situation on the Drujkivka front was partially stabilized, not the one near Dobropilla. This is the main place where Russia is currently advancing.

items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: The Canadian family that sold everything to chase Putin’s “traditional values” fantasy is now discovering what that visa actually buys you. After months of pressure, the patriarch faces a simple choice: sign a military contract and become fertilizer in a Ukrainian trench, or crawl back to Canada with nothing left. They burned their life savings cosplaying Little House on the Prairie in rural Russia. Now the Kremlin wants its payment in blood. Propaganda is cheap. The invoice always arrives later.

items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: Ukraine has built a fence that cuts drones out of the sky. The "Chaharnyk" system hears a fibre-optic drone pass overhead and severs the cable that controls it. Its makers claim a 95% success rate on any drone that flies over, New Scientist. 1/
